title: Full rational root span is equivalent to full coroot span
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and let $V,W$ be finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q$-vector spaces [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] in a perfect bilinear pairing $\langle-,-\rangle:V\times W\to\mathbf Q$, meaning that it identifies each space with the linear dual of the other. Let $a:I\hookrightarrow V$ and $b:I\hookrightarrow W$ be injective maps, with $\langle a_i,b_i\rangle=2$. Suppose that for each $i\in I$ there is a permutation $\sigma_i$ of $I$ satisfying $$a_{\sigma_i(j)}=a_j-\langle a_j,b_i\rangle a_i,\qquad b_{\sigma_i(j)}=b_j-\langle a_i,b_j\rangle b_i$$ for every $j\in I$, and that $\langle a_i,b_j\rangle\in\mathbf Z$ for every $i,j$. Thus these are the data of a finite crystallographic root pairing over $\mathbf Q$, without an assumption that either family spans. Then $$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\{a_i:i\in I\}=V\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\{b_i:i\in I\}=W.$$ Empty $I$ and zero-dimensional spaces are allowed.
